newsitem.title: FRANCE: St Gobain sees best annual performance.
newsitem.headline: St Gobain sees best annual performance.

text.p: Saint-Gobain chairman Jean-Louis Beffa said on Wednesday the glass maker was heading for over 100 billion francs in 1997 sales and higher profits in what would be easily its best ever annual performance.
The company would probably have a "significant rise" in net profits before capital gains, he told an annual shareholders' meeting.
Its 1996 revenue had been 91.4 billion francs.
"It now seems to me entirely likely that the group net profit, before capital gains, will show significant progress compared to 1996, both for the 1997 first half and for the full year," Beffa said.
The glass company posted net profit of 4.3 billion francs including capital gains, and 4.2 billion before capital gains.
"As elsewhere, capital gains from disposals were substantial...1997 will be clearly the best results in its (Saint-Gobain's) history," he said.
The "substantial" capital gains came mainly from the sale "in very good conditions" of the Cise group.

Last March, Beffa gave a more cautious forecast after a disappointing start to the year, with an estimate of an increase of at least 20 percent including capital gains. A source close to the company said this effectively meant a stable profit figure, if capital gains were stripped out.
"The start of the year was a bit disappointing," Beffa said. "January was bad, February was a little better. This situation led my first comments to consider the future with a certain prudence.
"I can say that the situation has changed favourably since then. March has show a clear recovery, which was confirmed in April, and May and June are on the same path," he said.
